title: Signature Consistent Hash Ring — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. A consistent hash ring assigns both servers and records to positions on a circle, and each record belongs to the first server clockwise from its position. Adding or removing a server only reassigns the records adjacent to it, instead of reshuffling everything the way naive modulo hashing does. Virtual nodes — many ring positions per physical server — smooth out load imbalances. This is the standard mechanism behind distributed caches and key-value stores for locating data without a central directory. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. Lineage: Signature-line counterpart of the public method of the same name, filed as a Signature original in the Signature archive.
provenance: JAH Databases archive-intelligence tools program, lane T2a — Signature original authored for Justin Addam Higgins.

title: Signature Request Routing — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. Once the ring says which node owns a record, the router forwards the request there — directly from the client when the ring is public, or through a coordinator when it is not. The router caches ownership decisions with a short TTL so repeated requests skip the ring computation. If the owning node is unreachable, routing fails over to the next node clockwise rather than failing the request. Clean routing keeps every node serving only its share, which is what lets the cluster scale horizontally. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. Lineage: Signature-line counterpart of the public method of the same name, filed as a Signature original in the Signature archive.

title: Signature Replica Quorum Reads — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. Important records are stored on several nodes, and a quorum read asks enough replicas that overlapping quorums guarantee the latest write is seen. With three replicas, reading from any two intersects every possible write quorum of two — the math that makes the system consistent without a master. The reader takes the value with the highest version stamp among the responses. Quorums let a distributed archive stay correct even while individual nodes lag or fail. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. Lineage: Signature-line counterpart of the public method of the same name, filed as a Signature original in the Signature archive.
demo:
REPLICAS = {"n1": ("v3", 3), "n2": ("v3", 3), "n3": ("v2", 2)}
QUORUM = 2
votes = list(REPLICAS.values())[:QUORUM]
best = max(votes, key=lambda v: v[1])
print("quorum of %d -> value %r at version %d" % (QUORUM, best[0], best[1]))

title: Signature Failover Handling — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. Nodes fail — disks die, networks partition — so the navigator treats every primary as temporary and every replica as a standby. Health checks mark dead nodes within seconds, and in-flight requests are retried against the next replica with the failure recorded for diagnosis. Writes during a failure go to surviving replicas and are reconciled when the node returns, using version stamps to order them. Failover done well is invisible: the archive keeps answering while the broken machine is repaired. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. Lineage: Signature-line counterpart of the public method of the same name, filed as a Signature original in the Signature archive.
provenance: JAH Databases archive-intelligence tools program, lane T2a — Signature original authored for Justin Addam Higgins.

title: Signature Locality-Aware Routing — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. When several replicas hold a record, the nearest one — same rack, same region, lowest measured latency — should answer. Locality-aware routing scores candidate replicas by recent round-trip times and picks the fastest, re-measuring continuously as conditions change. This cuts tail latency dramatically in geo-distributed archives, where a cross-ocean read can cost hundreds of milliseconds. The trade-off is mild load imbalance, corrected by capping how much extra traffic the nearest replica absorbs. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. Lineage: Signature-line counterpart of the public method of the same name, filed as a Signature original in the Signature archive.
demo:
RTT = {"us-east": 12, "us-west": 68, "eu": 95}
replicas = ["us-east", "us-west", "eu"]
best = min(replicas, key=lambda r: RTT[r])
print("nearest replica:", best, "(%d ms)" % RTT[best])
